\caption{Inclination-shallowing-corrected mean poles for the sedimentary units of the compilation; Table~\ref{tab:poles} gives the same poles as measured. Each is the mean of a \citet{Kent1982a} distribution whose 95\% confidence ellipse propagates the flattening-factor ($f$) uncertainty following \citet{Pierce2022a}. The ellipse is given as the mean pole, and the direction (longitude, latitude) and semi-angle of each of its axes, $\zeta_{95}$ for the major and $\eta_{95}$ for the minor. ``Correction'' gives the source of $f$: E/I \citep{Tauxe2004a} and SVEI \citep{Tauxe2024a} determine it from the directional distribution of the unit itself, whereas the compilation approach resamples flattening factors as compiled by \citet{Pierce2022a} (the median and 95$\%$ bounds are what is shown for those $f$ values). Scotland poles (Torridon, Stoer) are rotated into Laurentia coordinates before the paleolatitude of Duluth, Minnesota ($46.8^{\circ}$N, $267.9^{\circ}$E) is computed. That paleolatitude is repeated for the uncorrected pole of Table~\ref{tab:poles} alongside the corrected one; their bounds follow from $A_{95}$ and from the Kent ellipse along the Duluth-to-pole great circle.}\label{tab:kent_poles} \\
